title: Receipt Import to Inventory - Epic
description:
Import parsed receipt items into Core Data inventory, with support for:
- Creating new inventory from purchases
- Matching to existing inventory (with splitting logic)
- Deduplication when receipts are re-forwarded
- Price tracking per unit (weight or container)

title: Add rod count estimation from weight-based purchases
description:
When importing receipt items that are rods sold by weight, estimate the number of rods based on:
- Glass density (2.5 g/cm³)
- Rod dimensions by COE (length and diameter)
- Optional manufacturer-specific overrides

Create a RodEstimator utility that:
1. Looks up dimensions by COE (with manufacturer override support)
2. Converts weight units (oz, lb, g, kg) to grams
3. Calculates rod volume and weight
4. Returns estimated rod count (rounded to nearest int)
5. Calculates price per rod

COE defaults:
- COE 33 (boro): 20" (50.8cm), 7.5mm diameter
- COE 90/96/104 (soft): 12" (30.5cm), 5.5mm diameter

Location: Molten/Sources/Services/Receipt/ or Molten/Sources/Utilities/
acceptance_criteria:
- RodEstimator calculates rod count from weight
- Supports oz, lb, g, kg unit conversions
- Uses COE-based dimension defaults
- Structure ready for manufacturer overrides
- Returns nil/blank when calculation not possible
- Unit tests cover the math

title: PurchaseRecord deduplication service
description:
Create service logic to find existing PurchaseRecord when a receipt is re-imported.

Match by (in order of precedence):
1. `email_receipt_id` - exact match to server receipt ID
2. `order_number` + `supplier` + `date_purchased` (same day)
3. `sender_email` + `date_purchased` (same day) + approximate total match

If found, return existing record for update rather than creating duplicate.
acceptance_criteria:
- Service method to find existing PurchaseRecord by receipt metadata
- Returns nil if no match found
- Handles all three matching strategies

title: Consider adding account recovery mechanism for receipt imports
description:
Currently, if a user loses their security key (new device without iCloud Keychain, factory reset), they permanently lose:
1. Access to all unimported receipts
2. Their registered email address (stuck on orphaned account, 409 conflict on re-register)

This is a privacy-by-design tradeoff, but it creates a poor UX. Consider adding a recovery mechanism, such as:

Option A: Email-based key rotation
- If user has a verified email, allow them to request a "key rotation" via email verification
- Server sends verification link, user proves email ownership, server allows new public key to replace old one
- This would preserve user_id and all associated receipts

Option B: Release orphaned emails after timeout
- If an account has been inactive for X months and user tries to re-register the same email, allow it
- Old receipts would still be lost but at least email isn't permanently stuck

Option C: Manual support process
- Admin endpoint to migrate receipts between accounts after identity verification

The current behavior should at minimum be documented so users understand the risk before setting up.

title: Update PurchaseImportSheet UI for import flow
description:
Update the PurchaseImportSheet in PurchaseDetailView.swift to support the full import flow:

1. Add toggle/picker for "Add as new inventory" vs "Match to existing inventory"
2. Show preview of what will happen for each item
3. Handle partial match scenario - show prompt with three options:
   - Add N new items to reach receipt quantity
   - Add M new items (only the shortfall)
   - Note N-M as already consumed
4. Show progress during import
5. Show success/error states
acceptance_criteria:
- User can choose between add new vs match existing
- Partial match scenario shows clear options
- Import progress is visible
- Success/error feedback provided

title: Receipt import service - main orchestration
description:
Create main ReceiptImportService that orchestrates the full import flow:

1. Find or create PurchaseRecord (using deduplication service)
2. For each item being imported:
   - Create PurchaseRecordItem with catalog match and unit_price
   - Based on user choice:
     - "Add as new": Use InventoryTrackingService.addInventory(), then update StorageLocation with purchase link
     - "Match to existing": Use StorageLocation matching/splitting service

3. Handle partial match scenario - when existing inventory is less than receipt quantity:
   - Option A: Add new inventory for the difference
   - Option B: Add new to bring total up to receipt qty
   - Option C: Record shortfall as already consumed (create InventoryConsumptionRecord with unit_price)

4. Mark receipt as acknowledged on server after successful import
acceptance_criteria:
- Full import flow works end-to-end
- PurchaseRecord and PurchaseRecordItems created correctly
- StorageLocation records linked with purchase_record_item_id and unit_price
- Handles both "add new" and "match existing" flows
- Partial match prompts user and handles all three options

title: Core Data schema changes for receipt import
description:
Add new fields to Core Data entities for receipt import feature.

**PurchaseRecord** - add:
- `email_receipt_id` (String, optional) - server receipt ID for deduplication
- `sender_email` (String, optional) - for deduplication matching
- `order_number` (String, optional) - order ID from receipt

**PurchaseRecordItem** - add:
- `unit_price` (Decimal, optional) - price per unit

**StorageLocation** - add:
- `purchase_record_item_id` (UUID, optional) - links to the PurchaseRecordItem that created/claimed this inventory
- `unit_price` (Decimal, optional) - cost per unit at time of purchase

**InventoryConsumptionRecord** - add:
- `unit_price` (Decimal, optional) - cost per unit consumed (for partial match "already consumed" scenario)
acceptance_criteria:
- New model version created (Molten 30)
- All fields added to appropriate entities
- Migration path works from Molten 29

title: Audit error messages for userFacingMessage usage
description:
Review all error handling throughout the app and replace error.localizedDescription with error.userFacingMessage where appropriate. This ensures users get helpful recovery suggestions for errors like keyNotFound.

Key areas to check:
- Views that display errors from services
- Settings views
- Import/export operations
- Sync operations
- Any place that catches errors and displays them to users

The userFacingMessage extension is defined in KeyPairError.swift and provides enhanced messaging for KeyPairError cases, falling back to localizedDescription for other errors.

title: StorageLocation matching and splitting service
description:
Create service logic to find and split StorageLocation records for "match to existing" import flow.

**Finding matches:**
- Find StorageLocation records where Inventory.item_stable_id matches catalog item
- Filter to records where purchase_record_item_id IS NULL (not already linked)
- Prefer records with dateAdded >= order_datetime (closest first)
- Fall back to latest record before order_datetime if none found after

**Splitting logic:**
The split separates priced inventory from unpriced inventory:
- If matching record has MORE than needed: split into two records
  - New record: has the purchased quantity/containers, linked to purchase with unit_price
  - Original: keeps remainder, stays unlinked, no price
  - New record inherits dateAdded, locationName, inventoryId from original
- If exact match: just link and set price
- If LESS than needed across all locations: return available matches and shortfall amount

**Split across locations/dates:**
- Sort all matching records by closeness to order_datetime
- Consume from closest match first, then next closest, etc.
- Split individual records as needed
acceptance_criteria:
- Service can find unlinked StorageLocation records for an item
- Service can split a StorageLocation into priced/unpriced portions
- Splitting preserves original dateAdded on new record
- Works across multiple locations and dates

title: Server: return full datetime for order_date
description:
Update receipt-worker to return full ISO datetime (with time) for order_date instead of just the date portion.

Currently `extractOrderDate()` in parser.ts returns `date.toISOString().split('T')[0]` which strips the time.

Need full datetime for accurate matching when someone places multiple orders on the same day.
acceptance_criteria:
- order_date field includes time component (ISO 8601 format)
- iOS client parses full datetime correctly
